topics.topic: Handling of late, missed, or overlapping backup-look invocations and subsequent cadence
questions: When a scheduled call cannot run on time because the process is busy or suspended, is that call queued and made late, discarded, or coalesced with the next interval; and is the following interval anchored to the original schedule or to the late call?
If an invocation is still running, or the timer cannot execute at a scheduled boundary, are subsequent looks emitted concurrently, skipped, caught up, or delayed until 60 seconds after completion?
When one invocation lasts beyond the next scheduled interval or the scheduler runs late, are ticks fixed-rate, fixed-delay, coalesced, skipped, or allowed to invoke the capability concurrently?

quotes:
`module:instance_lifecycle` runs the look at the interval of the imported
`BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` constant, 60 seconds; `module:backups` applies the
03:00 and the retention, and decides nothing about when it is called.

1. **Due?** `capability:backups.run_daily_backup_if_due`, called by
   `module:instance_lifecycle` every `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS`, reads
   `capability:clock.recorded_now`. A run starts when an earlier look of this
   process saw this date before 03:00, the look is at or after 03:00, this
   process did not run this date, no run is going, and no kept backup of the
   date exists — a file whose record cannot be read counting as none (A18
   rule 1). The date is remembered, a failed run included.
judgement.why: The owner, capability, interval and non-overlap condition are named; queuing, coalescing, concurrency and fixed-rate versus fixed-delay timer mechanics are implementation notes owned by State 7.

topics.topic: Timing of the first backup look after instance startup
questions: Does `module:instance_lifecycle` call `capability:backups.run_daily_backup_if_due` immediately when the instance starts, or only after the first 60-second interval has elapsed?
When is the first look made after a successfully started instance begins serving, and what anchors later 60-second looks?
Is the first look made immediately when a service-token instance starts, or only after the first 60-second interval expires?

quotes:
6. **Start the passes.** Every 60 seconds from the start,
   `capability:owner_sessions.end_expired_sessions` (A13 rule 2). At least
   once a minute, `capability:backups.run_daily_backup_if_due`
   (`flow:daily_backup`), except in an owner-only start, which makes no
   backup run (A18 rule 9).

`module:instance_lifecycle` runs the look at the interval of the imported
`BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` constant, 60 seconds; `module:backups` applies the
03:00 and the retention, and decides nothing about when it is called.
judgement.why: State 4 names the timer owner and operation; whether an interval timer fires immediately at startup or after its first interval, and what anchors later ticks, are State 7 implementation notes.

topics.topic: Clock and suspension semantics for the 60-second backup-look interval
questions: Is the 60-second interval measured by elapsed monotonic time, by UTC wall-clock time, or by another timer whose behavior under wall-clock changes and suspension must be defined?
Which clock measures the interval, and does suspended time count so that a look is emitted immediately on resume?

quotes:
Any limit or schedule: the 8 hours, 30, 15 and 10 minutes and the 60 seconds
are `data_provider`'s constants that `owner_sessions` applies; the 03:00 is
one that `backups` applies; the minute look's 60 seconds is one that
`instance_lifecycle` applies, calling `backups` at that interval.

The limits of A13 are read by `owner_sessions` from `clock.monotonic_reading`;
the minute look of A18 rule 1 by `backups` from `clock.recorded_now`; a
backup's instant is the one `store` reads at the read that fixes the
copy's snapshot (A18 rule 1), which `backups` records and never reads
itself. No other module
reads a clock.
judgement.why: The texts assign the interval to `instance_lifecycle` and the due look's wall-clock reading to `backups`; the timer source and its suspension and wall-clock-adjustment mechanics are State 7 implementation notes.
